Minister orders urgent probe after mass fish deaths reported at Kilinochchi Tank

cards.what_happened: Fisheries Minister Ramalingam Chandrasegar has ordered an urgent investigation into mass fish deaths at Kilinochchi Tank. The directive followed a telephone discussion with Northern Province Governor Nagalingam Vedanayagam. Fish, freshwater prawns and juvenile fish reportedly died in the lower section of the tank.
details: Fisheries Minister Ramalingam Chandrasegar ordered an urgent probe after large numbers of fish, freshwater prawns and juvenile fish died in the lower part of Kilinochchi Tank. He issued the directive after speaking by telephone with Northern Province Governor Nagalingam Vedanayagam. The minister also called for a report on the incident.

Concerns have been raised over water-release procedures and possible problems during irrigation operations. Chandrasegar requested an assessment of financial losses suffered by freshwater fishing families who lost fish stocks and fishing equipment. An environmental assessment was also ordered to determine the impact on water quality and the surrounding ecosystem.
The minister said the causes of the fish deaths must be identified. He called for appropriate measures to provide relief to affected fishing communities.

He discussed the issue by telephone with Northern Province Governor Nagalingam Vedanayagam.
Fish, freshwater prawns and juvenile fish died in the tank's lower section.
Water-release procedures and irrigation operations are under concern.
Financial losses for freshwater fishing families will be assessed.
An environmental assessment will check water quality and ecosystem impact.
The minister wants causes identified and relief provided to fishing communities.

cards.spoken: Hello and welcome. Fisheries Minister Ramalingam Chandrasegar has ordered an urgent investigation after large numbers of fish, freshwater prawns and juvenile fish died in the lower section of Kilinochchi Tank. The minister made the decision after a telephone call with Northern Province Governor Nagalingam Vedanayagam. Authorities are worried about water-release procedures and possible issues during irrigation operations. The minister also wants an assessment of money lost by fishing families whose stocks and equipment were destroyed, plus an environmental check on water quality and the surrounding ecosystem. He has asked for the causes to be found and for relief to be provided to affected communities. A report on the incident has been requested. This is a developing story from Sri Lanka's Northern Province.

HRCSL orders probe into damage allegedly caused to Sigiriya Rock in 2017

cards.what_happened: The Sri Lanka Human Rights Commission ordered an investigation into damage allegedly caused to Sigiriya Rock during 2017 conservation work, after a petition by Deeman Ananda. The Commission found drilling, cable installation, and use of modern materials had damaged the rock, and directed several government bodies to take prompt action.
details: The Sri Lanka Human Rights Commission issued a determination on October 20 based on a petition filed by Deeman Ananda. The petition alleged that development and conservation work carried out at the Sigiriya World Heritage site in 2017 had destroyed archaeological evidence, including drilling holes, attaching machinery, altering the Lion’s Paw, and removing ancient inscriptions.

An on-site inspection found a cable system installed from the base to the summit to transport materials, with equipment attached to the rock. The rock had been drilled using electrical equipment, and modern mortar and cement were used in conserving ancient mortar. The Commission said the respondents — the Department of Archaeology, Central Cultural Fund, Ministry of Cultural Affairs, and the Sigiriya Project of the Central Cultural Fund — failed to prove the work had proper approval or followed formal procedure.

The Commission concluded the work caused damage to the rock, the most significant natural and cultural feature of Sigiriya, and warned that development without proper procedures could violate cultural and environmental heritage rights. However, the allegation that ancient inscriptions were removed could not be substantiated; the Department of Archaeology said only seven inscriptions had been identified in the area. The Commission stressed the need for a proper mechanism under joint supervision of the Department of Archaeology, the Cultural Triangle, and the National Building Research Organisation for activities of national importance, and made several recommendations to protect archaeological sites and preserve their historical value.
cards.why_it_matters: The Commission warned that development without proper procedures could violate rights relating to cultural and environmental heritage.

cards.spoken: Good morning. The Sri Lanka Human Rights Commission has ordered a full investigation into damage done to the iconic Sigiriya Rock. This follows a petition by Deeman Ananda, who said conservation work back in 2017 drilled holes into the rock, attached heavy machinery, and even altered the famous Lion’s Paw. Inspectors confirmed a cable system was run from the base to the summit, and modern cement was used on ancient mortar. The Commission found that the Department of Archaeology, the Central Cultural Fund, and other bodies could not prove the work had proper approval. They concluded the rock — the most significant natural and cultural feature of Sigiriya — was damaged, and warned that such unapproved development violates cultural and environmental heritage rights. The claim that ancient inscriptions were removed couldn’t be proven; only seven inscriptions are known in the area. Now the Commission has directed those agencies to act quickly and set up a joint supervision mechanism with the National Building Research Organisation for any future work of national importance.

16-year-old dies after car crashes into bus stop in Kohuwala

cards.what_happened: A 16-year-old died after a car went out of control and hit a bus stop on S. de S. Jayasinghe Mawatha in Kohuwala on Monday evening (Nov. 23). The car had been travelling from Nugegoda towards Kohuwala and hit a motorcycle and the rear of another car before striking the child at the bus stop. The child was taken to Colombo South Teaching Hospital in Kalubowila but died, and the 68-year-old driver was arrested.
details: Police said the car was going from Nugegoda towards Kohuwala when it lost control. It first hit a motorcycle and the back of another car. The car then hit the child, who was at a nearby bus stop, before hitting another motorcycle, a car and a van.

The child was seriously injured and was admitted to the Colombo South Teaching Hospital in Kalubowila. The child later died from the injuries. Three other people hurt in the accident were also admitted to the hospital.
The dead child was a resident of the Nugegoda area. The car driver, aged 68, is a resident of Morawila in Panadura and has been arrested. Kohuwala Police are carrying out further investigations.

First National Battery Testing Centre opened with Rs. 161.5 million investment

cards.what_happened: Sri Lanka inaugurated its first comprehensive national battery testing centre, the Centre for E-Mobility and Battery Technology, on Monday (Nov. 23) at the National Engineering Research and Development Centre. The facility was established under the patronage of Minister of Science and Technology Prof. Chrishantha Abeysena.
details: Sri Lanka opened its first comprehensive national battery testing centre, the Centre for E-Mobility and Battery Technology, at the National Engineering Research and Development Centre on Monday (Nov. 23). The inauguration was held under the patronage of Minister of Science and Technology Prof. Chrishantha Abeysena. Attendees included Ministry Secretary Dr. Roshanie Dissanayake, NERDC Chairman Dr. Chithral Ambawatte, Acting Director General Manoj Karunaratne and representatives of local and international industries.

The facility was established with a total investment of approximately Rs. 161.5 million, comprising Rs. 118 million from the Government's National Quality Infrastructure Strengthening Project and Rs. 43.5 million contributed by NERDC. It can assess battery performance, capacity, durability and safety under different environmental conditions, and also tests electric vehicle charging equipment and various battery systems.

The centre aims to expand Sri Lanka’s battery testing capabilities beyond conventional assessments to include modern battery technologies, supporting the development of electric mobility and renewable energy sectors. It will provide specialised testing services to local manufacturers, importers, researchers and technology developers, while supporting domestic product development and increasing local value addition.
